title: Objectwise quasi-isomorphism of direct-image K-injective resolutions
statement: Let $(C,J,A)$ and $(D,K,B)$ be small ringed sites in universe $u$, with commutative ring sheaves, as in [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $u:D\to C$ be continuous with left-exact inverse image on sheaves of sets, and $a:B\to u_*A$ a morphism of ring sheaves. Write $f_*$ for the induced module direct image [def-sfb-ringed-site-section-functors]. For every K-injective complex $I$ of $A$-module sheaves, every K-injective complex $T$ of $B$-module sheaves [def-pur-kinjective-complex], every quasi-isomorphism $j:f_*I\to T$, and every $V\in D$, the map $j(V):I(u(V))\to T(V)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of abelian groups after forgetting the section-ring action. Evaluation and module categories are those of [def-sfb-ringed-site-section-functors, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 0D6H (lemma-Leray-unbounded), proof of the second assertion; Tags 0D6G and 0D6E.

proof.text: Fix small ringed sites (C,A) and (D,B), a continuous u:D→C with left-exact sheaf pullback, and the structural ring map B→u_*A. Let I be K-injective, T K-injective, j:f_*I→T a quasi-isomorphism, and V in D. Localize at u(V) and V. The localized direct-image comparison identifies (f_*I)|V with (f_V)_*(I|u(V)). Restriction preserves K-injectivity and is exact, so j|V is a K-injective resolution.

source.place: Tag 0D6H (lemma-Leray-unbounded), proof of the second assertion; Tags 0D6G and 0D6E.

proof.text: On D/V the terminal object is id_V. Constant sheafification is left adjoint to evaluation there and preserves finite limits. The identity of B(V) gives the structural ring map from the constant B(V)-sheaf to B|V. This defines the punctual ringed-topos morphism p_V. The singleton module equivalence identifies its module direct image with evaluation at id_V.

source.place: Tag 0D6H (lemma-Leray-unbounded), proof of the second assertion; Tags 0D6G and 0D6E.

proof.text: Apply the K-injective-resolution normalization of derived direct-image composition to f_V followed by p_V. It says that (p_V)_*(j|V) is a quasi-isomorphism. Under the sectionwise identifications this map is j(V):I(u(V))→T(V). Forgetting the B(V)-action preserves cohomology, hence the corresponding map of abelian group complexes is a quasi-isomorphism. No preservation of K-injectives by f_* is used.

theorem leraySectionResolution_quasiIso
    {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D}
    (A : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (B : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{u})
    (u : D ⥤ C) [u.IsContinuous K J]
    (a : B ⟶ (u.sheafPushforwardContinuous CommRingCat.{u} K J).obj A)
    [PreservesFiniteLimits (u.sheafPullback (Type u) K J)]
    (I : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj A)) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective]
    (T : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose K (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj B)) ℤ) [T.IsKInjective]
    (j : ((SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u} (sectionModuleMap u a)).mapHomologicalComplex
      (.up ℤ)).obj I ⟶ T) [QuasiIso j] (V : D) :
    QuasiIso (((sectionEvaluation
      ((sheafCompose K (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj B) V).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)).map j)
